findings.reason: The parser still normalizes away empty operands before validating them, so malformed authorization expressions containing at least one non-empty capability are accepted instead of failing closed. For example, admin.access & becomes a single admin.access requirement, and | invoices.view becomes a single invoices.view requirement. A truncated conjunction can therefore silently drop an intended authorization constraint.

evidence.detail: Both methods call array_filter() to remove empty operands and only throw when the filtered array has count zero. Consequently, leading, trailing, or repeated operators with a non-empty neighbor bypass the new InvalidArgumentException checks.

findings.remediation: Validate every trimmed operand before filtering: reject the expression if any AND clause is empty, and reject each clause if any OR operand is empty. Preserve the existing rejection for wholly empty expressions.
findings.regressionTest: Add cases asserting InvalidArgumentException for capability &, & capability, capability && other, capability |, | capability, and capability || other, including at least one resolve() test using a malformed configured route permission.

coverage: Reviewed the complete embedded diff for RouteRequirementResolver and its unit tests.
Checked empty-expression handling across top-level AND parsing and per-clause OR parsing.
Checked the hash-bound red/green test evidence and discovered-test lists; the green evidence covers wholly empty expressions but not partially empty operands.
Checked public, null, missing-route, special-permission, single, ANY_OF, and ALL_OF paths for patch-related regressions.
